glance.what: Voice-driven generator of shader-rendered 3D landscapes using Gemini and GLSL.
glance.why: Lets anyone describe a world aloud and see it rendered instantly.

record.what_it_is: A web app where you speak a description and Gemini writes a GLSL shader that renders as a navigable 3D world in the browser, using retrieval over a database of Shadertoy snippets. You can keep speaking to refine the world and publish it to a gallery.
record.problem_and_user: Anyone, including people with dexterity limits, wanting to create real-time 3D graphics without writing shader code.
record.one_line_pitch: Speak a scene aloud and Gemini writes GLSL shader code that renders it as an interactive 3D visual, grounded by a shader-snippet RAG database.
record.problem_statement: Creating graphics shaders needs specialist code skill; the team wanted anyone to produce visuals just by describing them by voice.
record.devpost_tagline: Speak worlds into reality.
devpost_first_sections: We were hard at work figuring out what to build for Bitcamp , and after spending nearly a third of the competition in the ideation stage, we came up with VisuWorld . After combining some of the cool new tech we've explored - GLSL / Graphics, Google Gemini, and Voice to Text - we built VisuWorld!

Embarking on your own VisuWorld exploration begins with a speech to text prompt to Google's Gemini API, which generates GLSL code to represent just about anything that you can articulate out loud. Equipped with over 25,000+ graphics shader snippets in a RAG database, we've been able to see some truly impressive 3D visual landscapes over the course of this weekend.

glance.what: Study game that turns your notes into AI-made levels with a boss fight.
glance.why: Makes studying engaging for distractible learners.

record.what_it_is: Browser study game where uploaded lecture slides or notes become a question deck, then a sea-creature world: finish levels for pearls (XP), beat a practice-exam shark boss, and fight Pokemon-style AR duels by answering questions. Weak concepts spawn as stronger Storm variants.
record.problem_and_user: Students who get distracted by phones and find studying unmotivating.
record.one_line_pitch: Turns uploaded lecture material into a sea-creature study game with Pokemon-style AR duels, XP progression and a practice-exam boss.
record.problem_statement: Students procrastinate and lose focus while studying, so they need motivating, learning-style-adapted study tools.
record.devpost_tagline: A study game for dopamine-hungry brains: turn your notes into AI-made levels built for how you learn, beat the final boss, and battle friends in AR and grow from tiny krill into a mighty fish.
devpost_first_sections: We’ve all had those moments where we sit down to study, tell ourselves we’ll focus for an hour, and somehow end up scrolling on our phones five minutes later. As students, we’ve experienced the struggle with procrastination, short attention spans, and just finding the motivation to keep studying. We wanted to make studying feel less like something we had to force ourselves to do. Inspired by Pokémon GO, we created DopaMarine to turn studying into an interactive, real-world adventure where students can move, explore, and learn while also adapting to the way each person learns best.

DopaMarine turns your lecture slides, PDFs, and notes into a study game made for how you learn. You pick a sea-creature study buddy that matches your learning style. You earn pearls (XP) that allow you to pass levels and eventually beat the boss level — the big bad shark, which is the practice exam. Then take it into AR: open the virtual battlefield right through your phone’s camera and battle solo, against friends, or against players nearby in a Pokémon-style showdown. Each round shows a question from your notes, and you throw the ball with the correct answer to defeat your opponent’s avatar. The people you are competing with can either be studying the same or different things.

glance.what: Playful Frutiger Aero dance game with glossy cartoon characters.
glance.why: unclear

record.what_it_is: A Wii-style Frutiger Aero dance game in the browser: one or two players mimic on-screen dancers tracked by webcam or IoT camera and are scored on joint angles. An optional battle mode lets phone-scanning spectators send Solana devnet SOL to dancers, with results minted on-chain and texted via iMessage.
record.problem_and_user: Players who want a Just Dance or Kinect-like party game without console hardware, plus spectators who join dance battles from their phones.
record.one_line_pitch: Motion-tracked Frutiger Aero dance game for one or two players who copy on-screen dancers for points, with optional Solana-connected battles and QR-code join.
record.problem_statement: Dance games usually need dedicated hardware or consoles.
record.devpost_tagline: Frutiger Aero dance game on outdated IoT tech :)
devpost_first_sections: Aerodance was inspired by Just Dance-like games and systems like the Wii and Xbox Kinect.

Aerodance is a motion-tracked dance game in a Frutiger Aero style for one or two players. Players copy the moves of the dancers on screen and earn points based on how closely they match. Players also have the option to connect through Solana for dance battles. The players scan a QR code to join as dancers or as the crowd. The crowd can send the dancers SOL to hype them up mid-dance. Everyone will see the results by text. The phone number connected is the wallet for the users connected.

glance.what: Developer tool that orchestrates code inside a runtime, marionette-style.
glance.why: unclear

record.what_it_is: A terminal UI lets a developer add probes and prompt the agent.
record.problem_and_user: Frontend developers blocked by an unfinished backend, and developers wanting to test apps under simulated data and traffic.
record.one_line_pitch: Terminal tool that probes a running app, lets an LLM tamper with variables and simulate backend data so frontends are not blocked.
record.problem_statement: Frontend developers stall when the backend is unavailable and cannot test traffic or data realistically.
record.devpost_tagline: Bring your code to life. Orchestrate your code in the runtime.
devpost_first_sections: As a frontend engineer, if you are blocked by the backend, then your progress comes to a halt. With our tool, you can continue without interruption because it simulates traffic and data.

Puppeteer looks deeper into the runtime by probing into variables. It can change data on the fly. For example, in a frontend application, the database can act like it exists through our puppeteering approach.

glance.what: Autonomous agent that finds and exploits vulnerabilities in your codebase, live.
glance.why: Demonstrates security flaws in a live, visible way.

record.what_it_is: Command-line platform where several AI agents scan a codebase with static analyzers, plan a MITRE ATT&CK-style chain, run it against a disposable Docker target with a viewable desktop, then get defensive advice. It is a security-training and demonstration tool.
record.problem_and_user: Developers and security teams who get vulnerability lists but no proof of real-world impact; also learners studying red and blue team work.
record.one_line_pitch: A CLI that runs four AI agents to scan code, plan a MITRE ATT&CK kill chain, exploit an isolated Docker target and report defensive advice.
record.problem_statement: Static scanners list vulnerabilities without showing real exploitation, so learners and teams can't tell what LLM-claimed exploits actually work.
record.devpost_tagline: NARA autonomously discovers, plans, and exploits vulnerabilities in your codebase, powerful enough to get two of our team members banned from DevPost just for attempting to post it.
devpost_first_sections: Every cybersecurity course teaches you what vulnerabilities look like, but almost none show you what happens when they are actually exploited. Tools like Semgrep and Bandit are great at surfacing problems, but they hand you a list and leave the rest to imagination. We wanted to close that gap. When LLMs claim to find and exploit vulnerabilities, is it real, or just plausible-sounding output? We were inspired by the real-world red team / blue team dynamic. Most tools only do one. We wanted to build a full Red Team platform that does both: autonomously discover, plan, and exploit vulnerabilities programmatically, then turn around and advise on how to defend against them. NARA is an autonomous penetration testing CLI that orchestrates four AI agents against an isolated Docker target: Scanner - runs Semgrep and Bandit against a codebase (local path or GitHub URL), then uses an LLM to deduplicate and prioritize findings by exploitability, not just severity score. Planner - takes those findings and designs an ordered kill chain mapped to MITRE ATT&CK tactics, always ending with ransomware deployment as the final stage. Exploiter - provisions a disposable Docker container running Ubuntu 22.04 with an XFCE desktop, clones the vulnerable app inside it, then executes each kill chain step via docker exec. glance.what: Composer agent that turns hummed or spoken ideas into music-editing actions.
glance.why: Makes music creation accessible without musical skills.

record.what_it_is: Voice-to-MIDI composer: record humming, singing or beatboxing (optionally with spoken instructions), a multi-stage pipeline converts it to multi-track MIDI shown in a piano-roll editor, and further voice instructions edit the result through tool calls.
record.problem_and_user: Musically inclined people without instruments or production skills who want to turn a hummed idea into real music.
record.one_line_pitch: Agentic AI music tool that turns hummed or tapped musical ideas into produced tracks while keeping the artist in control.
record.problem_statement: Enthusiast musicians have melodies in their heads but lack a way to turn them into real music.
record.devpost_tagline: Everyone’s a composer now, hum it, say it, and we’ll build it! Orca the Composer Agent turns messy instructions into the exact tool actions to create or edit your track.
devpost_first_sections: Behind the Scenes of Orca

We're living in the golden age of creation. AI tools are unlocking creative potential like never before, but there's this massive gap: millions of enthusiast musicians and producers have incredible musical ideas stuck in their heads. You know that melody you hum in the shower? That beat you tap on your desk? Most people have no way to actually turn those into real music. We wanted to fix that. Our goal was simple: give musical enthusiasts the power to bring those fleeting melodies to life. Build something that keeps the artist in control while making the whole experience feel seamless and natural.

glance.what: Converts reward points into local vendor treats and deal alerts.
glance.why: Turns idle reward points into local deals and community.

record.what_it_is: Two-sided prototype for Revolut Points: consumers get personalised places to spend points from their transaction history, and small vendors upload a brochure so an AI agent drafts a marketing campaign. Includes a recruiter agent that enriches vendor leads and drafts outreach.
record.problem_and_user: Revolut customers rarely redeem points because they miss relevant offers; small partner vendors lack an automated way to reach interested users.
record.one_line_pitch: Streamlit prototype recommending where Revolut Points can be spent and letting vendors generate AI marketing campaigns from brochures.
record.problem_statement: Revolut points go unredeemed because users miss relevant vendors and small vendors lack reach.
record.devpost_tagline: Turn your RevPoints into local treats! Our platform connects users & small vendors with custom point rewards and alerts for trending deals, and building a local RevPoint community.
devpost_first_sections: Revolut users accumulate points but often fail to redeem them because they lack timely awareness of personally relevant opportunities. Discovering vendors that accept points requires manual searching and doesn't align with their actual spending habits or moments of purchase intent. This leads to points feeling disconnected, undervalued, and ultimately unused. Revolut partner vendors, particularly smaller ones, struggle to gain visibility among relevant user segments within the app. They lack an automated way to reach users whose demonstrated purchase history indicates a high likelihood of interest, especially users who are incentivized to spend (via points). The low redemption rate of Revolu

We built a system that analyzes a user's (simulated) transaction history (merchants, categories, potentially frequency/timing) to proactively recommend specific Revolut partner vendors where they can spend their points. Users can explore potential vendors offering discounts and reward programs in exchange for Revolut Points. We also created another interface to register new vendors in Revolut. We created a feature for small shop owners to upload pictures of their product catalogue and create a custom marketing campaign for them based on what categories of products users are frequently buying in similar places. We also notify interested users about these campaigns as soon as they are launched

glance.what: Map-based real estate platform with property analytics and market insights.
glance.why: Gives trustworthy property data to make faster decisions.

record.what_it_is: A property browsing app on a Google Maps interface where a Gemini assistant cross-checks listing data against live Google Search and assigns each property a trust score with a verification log. Includes favorites, compare, filters and analytics views.
record.problem_and_user: Home buyers and renters who cannot tell whether listing data is accurate or current.
record.one_line_pitch: Real estate browsing app with a Google Maps interface where a Gemini assistant fact-checks property data against Google Search and assigns each listing a trust score.
record.problem_statement: Consumers cannot tell whether online property listing information is reliable or current.
record.devpost_tagline: TrustEstate AI is your go-to for real estate. We use AI and enterprise-grade trust verification to deliver market insights and property analytics you can actually trust. Make smarter, faster decisions
devpost_first_sections: We came up with this concept since we saw how hard it is for consumers to find reliable real estate information online. Most property listings and platforms give users a lot of information, but they don't really say whether that information is reliable or even current. We wanted to build a platform that combines CBRE's data with AI that can do live fact-checking so that everyone can be sure of the choices they make when it comes to real estate. We wanted to make property research not just easier, but also smarter and safer.

Our app is a full-featured real estate helper that helps you find and trust properties. People may find properties using a Google Map interface that is both interactive and easy to use. Each property profile has more information than what is available to the public, thanks to CBRE's data. This includes prices, features, photos, past sales, and more. The app has a smart AI assistant that can answer inquiries, summarize insights or property histories, and, most significantly, check facts using real Google Search results. glance.what: AI drug discovery toolkit for designing and screening candidate molecules.
glance.why: Speeds up finding new drug molecules with AI models.

record.what_it_is: A modular starter toolkit that chains a generative molecule model, docking, binding-affinity prediction and embedding similarity search, backed by an ArangoDB biomedical knowledge graph and a GraphRAG layer. Ships as a notebook plus Streamlit app.
record.problem_and_user: Researchers facing slow, costly drug discovery where generative and in-silico models run in isolation; wants one extensible pipeline for new molecules and drug repurposing.
record.one_line_pitch: Modular agentic drug-discovery toolkit combining generative molecule models, binding prediction and an ArangoDB biomedical knowledge graph with GraphRAG retrieval.
record.problem_statement: Drug discovery is slow and costly, and generative, scoring and knowledge tools are not integrated into one end-to-end candidate pipeline.
record.devpost_tagline: NeuThera is an AI-driven drug discovery toolkit integrating multiple SOTA generative models for de novo molecular design. Combines graph-based retrieval with advanced compound fingerprint embeddings.
devpost_first_sections: NeuThera - AI-Driven Drug Discovery Toolkit

Traditional drug discovery methods are hindered by high costs, long timelines upwards of 20 years, and a high attrition rate in clinical trials. With the rise of AI and computational biology -- Generative models and in-silico validation techniques have shown promise in accelerating early-stage drug design. However, current models often operate independently of each other, lacking an integrated pipeline for end-to-end drug candidate generation. glance.what: AI note-taking assistant plus an API for building AI products.
glance.why: Promises efficiency and new revenue through AI note-taking.

record.what_it_is: AI note-taking web app that transcribes lectures live, lets users edit notes with natural-language commands, turns descriptions into Mermaid diagrams, and answers questions through a voice assistant. Notes can be shared by link or exported to PDF.
record.problem_and_user: Students and developers who struggle to take organized notes during lectures and technical discussions with ordinary note apps.
record.one_line_pitch: AI note-taking app with real-time lecture transcription, natural-language editing, diagram generation, sharing, PDF export and a voice assistant.
record.target_user: Students and developers taking lecture notes
record.problem_statement: Traditional note apps cannot organise or enhance content intelligently during live lectures and technical talks.
record.devpost_tagline: Capture Ideas, Create Clarity, Powered by AI.
devpost_first_sections: As students and developers, we've experienced firsthand the challenges of taking effective notes during lectures and technical discussions. Traditional note-taking apps lack the intelligence to help organize and enhance content in real-time. We envisioned Notable as a bridge between conventional note-taking and AI-powered assistance, inspired by the potential of large language models to understand and enhance educational content.

Notable is an intelligent note-taking application that transforms how users capture and interact with information. It features real-time lecture transcription, AI-powered content enhancement, and automatic diagram generation from text descriptions. Users can edit their notes using natural language commands, share notes with unique links, export them to PDF format, and even generate diagrams. The app also includes a context-aware voice AI assistant that can answer questions about the notes and suggest improvements to the content.

glance.what: Web app to register your CUPRA Tavascan and explore its features.
glance.why: Helps drivers discover everything about their new car.

record.what_it_is: A web platform for prospective Cupra Tavascan buyers: a manual-grounded RAG chatbot, an image upload and region-select flow that explains car parts, object detection with labels, and an interactive 3D interior in a Cupra-styled interface.
record.problem_and_user: Prospective and new Cupra Tavascan owners who want to know the car before it is theirs; answers drawn from the official manual rather than free generation.
record.one_line_pitch: Web platform where prospective Cupra Tavascan buyers chat, upload photos and tour a 3D interior, answered from the car manual.
record.problem_statement: Owners and buyers struggle to learn car features from a long PDF manual.
record.devpost_tagline: A web to further understand the incredible capabilities of technology applied to the new Cupra car. Know your car before it is even yours. A solution to the SEAT challenge at HackUPC.
devpost_first_sections: We took on the SEAT challenge because we felt a personal drive to push ourselves and to test the limits of our knowledge, which a project like this one might surely do.

We developed an intuitive and intelligent platform that helps potential buyers interact with and explore the Cupra Tavascan. Through a combination of conversational interfaces, image understanding, and immersive visualization, users can get to know the car in a more engaging and informative way.

glance.what: Maps a product's global supply chain from raw materials to delivery.
glance.for_whom: Supply chain analysts and curious consumers
glance.why: Makes hidden global supply chains visible.

record.what_it_is: [redacted]
record.problem_and_user: People curious how everyday products are made, since the route from raw materials to finished goods is hard to see.
record.one_line_pitch: Web app where a product name is expanded by GPT into raw materials, components and industrial hubs shown on an interactive globe map and flow diagram.
record.problem_statement: Supply chains behind everyday products are hidden and complex.
record.devpost_tagline: From raw materials to finished good – now visualised.
devpost_first_sections: The grand adventures of mythology might seem distant, but a far more impressive journey unfolds every day – the complex supply chains that bring the products we use to our hands. From raw materials to finished goods, a single smartphone or pair of shoes traverses continents, undergoing incredible transformations. This project explores that journey.

SupplyTrace is a web application that generates interactive supply chain visualisations. Users input a product, and the application deconstructs it into its raw materials, refinement processes, and components, geographically linking each to its most likely industrial hub. The results are presented on an interactive global map, highlighting the intricate network that connects resources, factories, and consumers. An accompanying flow diagram provides an alternative view of the supply chain, further enhancing understanding.

glance.what: Chat-based reading tool that makes reading active; cover is only a logo.
glance.why: Makes reading more active and engaging.

record.what_it_is: A voice-first AI tutor that ingests a student's notes, PDFs or photos, then teaches Socratically by speech while drawing notes and visuals on an infinite Tldraw whiteboard, backed by a LangGraph agent, Gemini and a Qdrant vector store.
record.problem_and_user: Students who study passively from their own notes and benefit from guided questioning and active recall.
record.one_line_pitch: Voice-first multimodal AI tutor that takes uploaded notes or photos and teaches through Socratic questions, analogies and visuals on an infinite whiteboard.
record.problem_statement: Students studying alone lack an interactive tutor that works from their own materials and explains visually.
record.devpost_tagline: No more passive reading, just active chats! - AGORA
devpost_first_sections: We believe active recall and guided discovery are far more effective than passive reading. We were inspired by the Socratic method to build an AI tutor that doesn't just give answers but asks the right questions.

Agora is a voice-first, multimodal AI tutor that you study with. You upload your notes, PDFs, or even photos of your lecture scribbles, and then talk to the tutor via a push-to-talk interface. It guides you through complex topics with Socratic questions, live analogies, and visual explanations on an infinite blackboard, all while tracking your "confused" topics to generate quizzes later.

glance.why: Catches service regressions between versions before release.

record.what_it_is: An API regression tool that compares two versions of an API, flags structural and semantic differences, has Nemotron generate and run test cases, and has Gemini explain regressions and suggest fixes. Results appear in a dashboard with heatmaps and health scores.
record.problem_and_user: QA engineers, DevOps and backend developers who manually diff JSON and write tests when API versions change.
record.one_line_pitch: AI-assisted API regression tool that diffs two API versions, auto-generates tests and explains breaking changes with visual health dashboards.
record.problem_statement: Debugging breaking changes between API versions is slow and manual for QA and backend teams.
record.devpost_tagline: qAPIbara — AI-Powered Regression Testing
devpost_first_sections: 🧩 qAPIbara Version Smarter. Debug Faster.

APIs evolve fast—but debugging breaking changes, regressions, or inconsistencies between versions is slow, repetitive, and often manual. QA engineers spend hours testing the same endpoints, comparing JSONs, and writing endless test cases that could be automated. We built qAPIbara to transform API regression testing into an intelligent, explainable, and predictive process—bridging the gap between development speed and testing reliability. glance.what: Visual cloud architecture designer with instant cost estimates.
glance.why: Shows cloud costs before you build the architecture.

record.what_it_is: Cost-intelligence tooling for developers: a VS Code extension that flags expensive API calls in code with a heatmap and one-click cheaper fixes, plus a web sandbox for sketching architectures and forecasting their costs.
record.problem_and_user: Developers and teams surprised by API, database and cloud bills that stay invisible until the invoice.
record.one_line_pitch: VS Code extension and web dashboard that flag costly AI API calls in code, suggest cheaper models and forecast spend.
record.target_user: developers and engineering teams using AI APIs
record.problem_statement: AI API costs are invisible to developers until the invoice arrives, causing surprise bills.
record.devpost_tagline: The first linter for your budget. Real-time cost intelligence for your IDE and a predictive sandbox for your architecture.
devpost_first_sections: Innovation shouldn't come with a surprise bill. As developers rushing to build the next big thing, we often treat AI as a magic wand. But unlike memory or CPU cycles, AI API calls cost real money—and those costs are currently invisible until the invoice arrives. We realized that to truly innovate sustainably, engineers need financial intuition built directly into their tools. Whether you're a bootstrapper protecting your runway or an enterprise scaling a unicorn, you can't afford to be blind to your burn rate. Quota was born to make cost a first-class citizen in the development lifecycle, bridging the gap between "move fast" and "don't go broke."

Quota is a real-time financial intelligence suite for modern engineering. It catches "financial bugs" before they ship. glance.what: Rhythm game that teaches American Sign Language through play.
glance.why: Makes learning sign language fun and engaging.

record.what_it_is: Rhythm game that teaches ASL fingerspelling: a webcam reads hand landmarks with MediaPipe, a MobileNetV2 model classifies the letter A to Z, and the player must sign letters as notes hit a Guitar Hero style highway, with training, testing and arcade modes.
record.problem_and_user: Few hearing people can sign ASL; the project targets hearing learners who want a fun way to practise fingerspelling.
record.one_line_pitch: Guitar Hero-style rhythm game that teaches ASL fingerspelling using webcam hand tracking, with song, training and testing modes.
record.problem_statement: Learning sign language fingerspelling is dull and gives little real-time feedback.
record.devpost_tagline: Compete, have fun, and master ASL, one beat at a time.
devpost_first_sections: SignHero 🤟

Over 48 million Americans are deaf or hard of hearing, yet ASL literacy remains low among the hearing population. We wanted to make learning ASL fingerspelling fun, accessible, and engaging —the same way Guitar Hero made learning rhythm patterns addictive. The breakthrough idea: What if we could gamify sign language learning with real-time AI detection and rhythm-based gameplay?

glance.what: Sustainability app giving habit insights and rewards for eco choices.
glance.why: Rewards planet-friendly habits so people act sustainably.

record.what_it_is: Sustainability app that tracks a user's purchases through uploaded receipts, scores companies on ESG, and offers 2% cash back on buying from qualifying companies.
record.problem_and_user: Greenwashing makes it hard for consumers to know whether purchases are really sustainable.
record.one_line_pitch: Sustainability app with receipt-upload ESG tracking, resources to plan and learn, and cash-back style incentives meant to counter greenwashing.
record.problem_statement: Companies overstate environmental efforts, and consumers lack easy ways to track and be rewarded for sustainable habits.
record.devpost_tagline: Make informed choices that positively impact the planet. Improve habits with actionable insights while gaining rewards.
devpost_first_sections: Our inspiration came from a recent article about greenwashing 📰—a practice where companies overemphasize their environmental efforts to promote growth and increase profits.

We encourage users to adopt sustainable practices by offering resources to plan, track, and learn about sustainability. 🌟 Incentives like 2% cash back 💵 for meeting company sustainability standards and an easy-to-use ESG tracker through receipt uploads 📸 motivate customers to improve their habits.

glance.what: AI-guided 3D immersive learning environments for historical periods.
glance.why: Makes history learning immersive rather than passive.

record.what_it_is: A web app where a user types a historical event or science concept, a 3D Gaussian-splat world is generated, and a voiced AI guide answers questions about what is in the scene. A STEM mode adds guided experiments.
record.problem_and_user: Learners (history and science) for whom textbooks are passive; wants to show rather than tell.
record.one_line_pitch: Type a historical event or science concept and explore a generated 3D world with a voiced AI guide that answers questions about the scene.
record.target_user: students and learners of history and STEM
record.problem_statement: Textbook learning of history and science is passive; students are told rather than shown.
record.devpost_tagline: 3D learning environments for the modern era.
devpost_first_sections: Education has always struggled to make history and science feel real. Reading about life in an Ancient Chinese Village or how photosynthesis works in a textbook is passive. You're told what happened/happens, not shown it. We were inspired by the idea that immersive 3D environments could transform learning from memorization into genuine exploration, and that an AI guide embedded inside those worlds could answer questions the way a knowledgeable human standing next to you would.

Atlas lets you type any historical event or scientific concept and instantly step inside a generated 3D world built around it. Once inside, an AI Guide speaks and responds to your questions in real time, grounding every answer in the specific scene you're exploring. You can click on individual objects to focus on them, ask follow-up questions, and for STEM scenes, interact with guided experiments like a photosynthesis cycle that responds to your actions.

glance.what: Phone app that narrates surroundings aloud, live, for blind users.
glance.why: Helps visually impaired people navigate their surroundings safely.

record.what_it_is: A phone web app that narrates the camera view in short spoken language, paired with an ESP8266 ultrasonic sensor clamped on a cane that sends distance over Wi-Fi and is turned into variable-frequency beeps. Users can also ask questions about what is ahead and have text read aloud.
record.problem_and_user: Visually impaired students and pedestrians whose cane detects only nearby obstacles; cites mobility-injury survey data from campus experience.
record.one_line_pitch: Phone-camera scene narration plus an ultrasonic cane attachment that turns obstacle distance into beeps, helping visually impaired people navigate.
record.problem_statement: Mobility canes give limited information, and visually impaired people suffer frequent injuries from hazards and head-level obstacles.
record.devpost_tagline: Narrating the world for the visually-impaired.
devpost_first_sections: Our inspiration came from a teammate who witnessed his dormmate, who was visually impaired, struggling to navigate campus using only a mobility cane. Although his cane helps detect nearby obstacles, it provides limited information about the surrounding environment, making independent navigation challenging. [Research] shows that 7% of visually impaired and/or blind respondents experienced non-superficial injuries every month due to hazards and trips. Furthermore, 13% of respondents reported having head-level injuries that resulted in stitches and dental care every month. These experiences inspired us to develop technology that helps our community members with visual impairments to detect obs

SonoRocky includes two major elements: 1) Our Vision-to-Language application, and 2) a Mobility Cane System to detect distances. devpost_first_sections: Someone we know has Parkinson’s disease, and like many patients, he suffers from Freezing of Gait (FOG) — a sudden, involuntary inability to walk. Recent research (N.E. Ibrahim, Nature, 2024) has shown that targeted muscle stimulation can effectively eliminate FOG. Inspired by this, his family noticed that gently poking the back of his leg with a stick during an episode helped him move again. This simple action inspired us to develop an automated, predictive solution.

Our project, pFOG, is a wearable device that predicts Freezing of Gait using sensor data and machine learning. We also built a web interface for easy data collection and labeling, which allows users to fine-tune a model using their own walking data—essential for adapting to gait variability across patients.

devpost_first_sections: We wanted to build a project using hardware and agentic AI to filter though data. We figured it would be a creative way to gather and make decisions based on data. Seeing the results in person, on an Arduino, puts into perspective what is possible with hardware and agentic AI.

HealthSense has 3 sensors: an accelerometer, a heart rate monitor, and a temperature sensor. The Arduino constantly checks the three sensors and sends the data to the Raspberry Pi 5. The Pi 5 then sends the data to Redis. Vultr is used to hold the Redis database and runs the Nemotron Agentic AI. The AI is used to make decisions based on the previous data and most recent data. If the most recent data is concerning, the AI sends an alert to the person wearing the sensors by vibrating a sensor. The person can say they are perfectly fine by clicking a button to turn off the vibrating sensor.
